rubric_items.reason: All four ticket acceptance criteria map to REQ-1, REQ-2, REQ-4, REQ-5; job cadence is listed under Out of scope with a reason.
REQs are atomic; REQ-6 and REQ-16 use the vague 'within the one day' instead of the 24h-after-start rule fixed by A-02.
Every REQ cites the ticket or an IDE answer; REQ-9 (cancel a Stale appointment) reads 'cancel' into A-03's 'close', which is a stretch given the Cancelled definition.
The Scheduled-only-can-change clash was asked (A-03) with a mismatch; the clash with the glossary Cancelled definition (before it took place) was not raised.
Questions had real options and defaults, were answered in the IDE, and Q-05 was correctly non-blocking.
Plain and readable; glossary terms used consistently, with 'reschedule (move)' bridged to the glossary wording.

findings.text: REQ-9 lets staff cancel a Stale appointment (at least 24h past start) and REQ-6 cancels past appointments, but the glossary defines Cancelled as called off before it took place. This clash is not asked or recorded as a mismatch.

cites.quote: Staff can still cancel a Stale appointment `with a reason`.
An appointment called off before it took place, with a reason
answer: Staff can still close or reschedule it (proposed default)

findings.suggested_fix: Ask whether cancelling a past/Stale appointment is allowed despite glossary#cancelled, citing both sides; or record it in A-03's mismatch if the user confirms.

findings.text: REQ-6 and REQ-16 say 'within the one day' while A-02 fixed the window as 24h after the start time, as REQ-4 and REQ-5 state.

cites.quote: An appointment cancelled within the one day is no longer `Scheduled` and is not marked Stale.

findings.suggested_fix: Word REQ-6 and REQ-16 as 'within 24h after its start time'.

cites.quote: closed by staff once its start time has passed
